# Loops Requirements Review Checklist: Reusable Development Loops

**Purpose**: An author self-review of requirements quality across execution and safety, validation
and evidence, and inputs, reusability, and orchestration, before `/speckit-tasks`
**Created**: 2026-09-27
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) (cross-checked against [plan.md](../plan.md),
[research.md](../research.md), and [data-model.md](../data-model.md))

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

Each item is followed by a **Recommended fix**: a suggested change to the requirements text. The
fixes are proposals only; they have not been applied. Applying one is the author's decision, for
example through `/speckit-clarify` or by editing the spec directly.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 - Does the spec bound *planning* attempts, or does only milestone work have a trial limit? [Gap, Spec §FR-005, Spec §FR-028]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add an FR stating that invalid or unusable planning output counts as a
    planning trial under the same `max_trials` limit. Exhausting those trials ends the run as
    `stopped-on-failure` (this matches plan R-5).
- [ ] CHK002 - Are per-call safeguards (a hung or runaway Claude Code call) specified as stopping conditions, beyond the trial count? [Gap, Constitution V]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add an FR requiring a configurable per-call time limit and a configurable
    per-run call cap, where reaching either is a recorded failure. Leave the values to
    configuration (plan R-18).
- [ ] CHK003 - Does the spec define what a developer may do after `stopped-on-failure`, or is the workspace permanently closed? [Gap, Spec §FR-028, Plan U-5]
  - **Recommended fix**: Settle U-5 in the spec. Either add "a developer MAY explicitly grant a new
    trial budget to one failed milestone; the grant, its reason, and its time MUST be recorded", or
    state that a stopped workspace is final and work continues in a new workspace.
- [ ] CHK004 - Is it specified whether an interrupted trial counts toward the trial limit? [Gap, Spec §FR-030, Plan U-2]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add one sentence to FR-005 or FR-030: "A trial interrupted before its
    result is recorded counts as a failed trial with reason *interrupted*." Alternatively, state
    the opposite explicitly.
- [ ] CHK005 - Are requirements defined for two runs attempting to use the same workspace at the same time? [Gap, Spec §FR-049]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add an FR: "Only one loop run MAY be active per workspace. A second run
    MUST refuse to start and report the active run."
- [ ] CHK006 - Does the spec require every task and acceptance criterion to trace back to a requirement reference in the input? [Gap, Constitution VIII, Spec §FR-014]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add an FR: "Every planned task and acceptance criterion MUST cite at least
    one requirement or story identifier from the input." The plan already enforces this (R-5).
- [ ] CHK007 - Does the spec say how Claude Code service failures (API error, rate limit, expired login) are classified: a failed trial that uses up the budget, or an infrastructure stop? [Gap, Exception Flow]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add an edge case and an FR. Recommended wording: "A call that fails for
    reasons outside the work, such as service unavailable or authentication, MUST stop the run with
    a distinct recorded reason and MUST NOT consume a trial."

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK008 - Is the "3rd trial" wording in FR-005 consistent with the configurable limit in FR-006? [Clarity, Conflict, Spec §FR-005, Spec §FR-006]
  - **Recommended fix**: Reword FR-005 to say "fails validation on its final trial (the configured
    trial limit, default 3)".
- [ ] CHK009 - Is "content identity" in FR-051a defined precisely enough to say whether a whitespace-only edit counts as a change? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-051a]
  - **Recommended fix**: State that identity is byte-level ("any byte change is a change"), or
    define the normalization. Byte-level matches plan R-5/data-model (SHA-256) and is simplest.
- [ ] CHK010 - Is "token consumption" defined with specific counters, such as input, output, and cached tokens? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]
  - **Recommended fix**: In FR-004, list the recorded figures as input, output, cache-creation, and
    cache-read tokens, plus cost where available, each summed over all calls of the milestone.
- [ ] CHK011 - Are a milestone's "start time" and "end time" defined when the milestone spans several runs or interruptions? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]
  - **Recommended fix**: Define start as the start of the milestone's first trial and end as the end
    of its last validation. Also require the time of each trial to be recorded (data-model:
    Milestone).
- [ ] CHK012 - Is "the prompt used for each milestone" (FR-033) clear, given that a milestone involves several Claude calls? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-033]
  - **Recommended fix**: Reword it as "the session ID and full prompt of **every** Claude Code call,
    tagged with its milestone and trial".
- [ ] CHK013 - Is the role of optional unit tests in the pass or fail decision stated, when they are enabled and fail while curl or Playwright pass? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-008]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add: "When unit tests are enabled for a run, a failing unit-test run MUST
    fail the milestone's validation. When they are disabled, they have no effect."

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK014 - Do the spec's remaining open questions (Q-6, Q-7, Q-8) and the phrase "depends on Q-7" in FR-001 still match the plan, which has since decided them? [Consistency, Spec §Open Questions, Spec §FR-001, Plan DR-16/17]
  - **Recommended fix**: Record the plan's decisions in the spec as D-9 (sequential orchestration),
    D-10 (`task.md` template plus a rendered copy per run), and D-11 (tokens from Claude Code's
    per-call usage report). Remove the "depends on Q-7" note from FR-001.
- [ ] CHK015 - Is FR-035a's "each run MUST be given a target project directory" consistent with the plan's separate backend and frontend targets under the orchestrator? [Conflict, Spec §FR-035a, Plan §Optional orchestration]
  - **Recommended fix**: Reword FR-035a to "each **loop run** MUST be given a target directory". Add
    that the backend and frontend loops of one application MAY use different targets, and that
    neither may write to the other's.
- [ ] CHK016 - Is the unit terminology consistent? FR-014, FR-017, and FR-020 say "phase", while trials and accounting use "milestone". [Consistency, Spec §A-2]
  - **Recommended fix**: Choose "milestone" as the canonical term. Change "phase" to "milestone" in
    the FRs, and keep A-2's note once: "(called 'phase' in the task description)".
- [ ] CHK017 - Is FR-034 ("state wins on disagreement") backed by a requirement, or does it rest only on assumption A-3? [Consistency, Assumption, Spec §FR-034, Spec §A-3]
  - **Recommended fix**: Promote A-3 into FR-034: "`state/` is the authoritative record; the phase
    files and `progress.md` are derived views." Then delete A-3.
- [ ] CHK018 - Does SC-007 (the reference application passes all checks) conflict with Out of Scope, which excludes the reference application's code and tests? [Conflict, Spec §SC-007, Spec §Out of Scope]
  - **Recommended fix**: Mark SC-007 as a *consumer-phase acceptance criterion*: "measured when the
    loops are applied to the reference application; not a deliverable of this feature". Keep a
    fixture-based end-to-end criterion for this feature (see CHK024).

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK019 - Can "unrelated application domains" in SC-006 be judged objectively? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
  - **Recommended fix**: Define "unrelated" measurably. For example: the two requirement documents
    share no entities or endpoints and need different milestone plans.
- [ ] CHK020 - Is SC-008 ("a developer who has never used the loops … using only the README") testable without a subjective judgement? [Measurability, Spec §SC-008]
  - **Recommended fix**: Replace it with a scripted walkthrough: "Following only the README's
    commands, each loop and the orchestrator reach `completed` on the smoke fixture with no steps
    beyond those documented."
- [ ] CHK021 - Does the spec require every acceptance criterion of a milestone to be covered by at least one validation check? [Gap, Spec §FR-018, Spec §FR-023]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add: "A milestone's validation MUST produce a result for every one of its
    acceptance criteria. A criterion with no result counts as failed." The plan's pass rule already
    does this.
- [ ] CHK022 - Is "observable UI behavior" in FR-023 defined with a minimum evidence standard, such as the observed text or state, or a screenshot per criterion? [Clarity, Spec §FR-023]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add: "Each UI criterion result MUST include what was observed and at least
    one stored evidence item."

## Validation and Evidence Coverage

- [ ] CHK023 - Does the spec address the risk that the same Claude session writes the code, writes its tests, and judges the result? [Gap, Spec §FR-027]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add an FR: "Validation checks MUST NOT be weakened after the first trial of
    a milestone, and pass or fail MUST be decided from recorded evidence, not from the
    implementer's own claim." Keep the mechanism (frozen checks, a separate read-only step) in the
    plan.
- [ ] CHK024 - Is there an end-to-end acceptance criterion for this feature that does not depend on the reference application? [Gap, Spec §Success Criteria]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add SC-011: "Both loops reach `completed` on a minimal smoke requirement,
    and the orchestrator also completes it, with every milestone showing passing validation
    evidence."
- [ ] CHK025 - Is FR-019 ("the Swagger document describes only implemented and verified endpoints") consistent with when the document is read? It is updated during a milestone, before that milestone is verified. [Consistency, Spec §FR-019]
  - **Recommended fix**: Scope FR-019 to the published artifact: "The Swagger document handed to
    `frontend-dev` MUST describe only endpoints verified in achieved milestones."
- [ ] CHK026 - Is it specified whether the Swagger deliverable is only a document, or must also be served as an interactive page (U-1)? Is its format required? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-016, Plan U-1]
  - **Recommended fix**: Settle U-1 in FR-016. Recommended wording: "an OpenAPI 3 document in a
    machine-readable format; serving an interactive page is optional."
- [ ] CHK027 - Does the spec define how `frontend-dev` gets a reachable backend when it runs directly, without the orchestrator? [Gap, Spec §FR-039, Plan U-3]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add to FR-039: "When run directly, `frontend-dev` MUST accept either the
    address of a running backend or instructions for starting one. Without either, criteria that
    need a backend MUST fail, never pass silently."

## Inputs, Reusability and Orchestration

- [ ] CHK028 - Are requirements defined for a single story that depends on another story that has not been implemented yet? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-010a]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add an edge case. The loop records the dependency as an open question at
    the planning pause. It MUST NOT implement the other story (this is consistent with D-4 and
    FR-010a).
- [ ] CHK029 - Does FR-013 require the Swagger input to be structurally valid, and not just present and readable? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013, Spec §FR-011]
  - **Recommended fix**: Extend FR-013: "For `frontend-dev`, an API specification that cannot be
    parsed as an OpenAPI document MUST stop the run with an input error."
- [ ] CHK030 - Are the approval steps fully specified: how answers are provided, and whether answers can trigger replanning or only become context? [Clarity, Spec §FR-053, Plan R-6]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add to FR-053: "The developer MAY either approve (the answers become binding
    context) or request replanning with the answers (the loop pauses again). Both actions and the
    answers MUST be recorded."
- [ ] CHK031 - Is the answers file covered by change detection? Is editing answers after approval allowed or detected? [Gap, Spec §FR-051a, Spec §FR-054]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add the approved answers to the inputs that FR-051a fingerprints, so an
    edit after approval stops the run the same way a requirements change does (D-8).
- [ ] CHK032 - Is FR-055's "record an assumption and continue" limited when the assumption would change scope materially, for example adding a feature or dropping a requirement? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-055]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add: "An assumption that removes, adds, or contradicts a requirement MUST
    NOT be made after approval. The milestone fails with reason *needs-input* instead."

## Non-Functional Requirements and Boundaries

- [ ] CHK033 - Does the write boundary (FR-035b) state which paths outside the target are allowed, such as dependency caches, temporary files, and browser downloads? Without that, installing packages breaks the rule. [Edge Case, Conflict, Spec §FR-035b, Spec §SC-009]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add an explicit allowance for tool-managed caches and system temporary
    directories. Scope SC-009 to "the repository and other project directories".
- [ ] CHK034 - Are requirements defined for secrets or credentials that may appear in recorded prompts, curl responses, or evidence? [Gap, Security]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add an NFR: "Loops MUST NOT write secrets named in configuration into
    state, evidence, or prompts. Workspaces containing evidence MUST be reviewable before they are
    committed." At minimum, list this as an explicit exclusion.
- [ ] CHK035 - Is the permission level that automated implementation steps run with specified or deliberately left to the plan (U-4)? [Gap, Security, Plan U-4]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add a principle-level FR: "Automated steps MUST run with the least tool
    permissions their step needs, and permission to change files MUST be limited to the loop's
    target." Keep the specific modes in the plan.
- [ ] CHK036 - Are performance and time targets intentionally excluded, and is that exclusion stated? [Completeness, Non-Functional]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add to Out of Scope: "No performance or duration targets for loop runs in
    this feature, beyond the configurable limits."

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK037 - Is A-1 (Claude Code, the Playwright MCP server, and curl are available) paired with a required behavior when a dependency is missing at run time? [Assumption, Spec §A-1, Spec §FR-013]
  - **Recommended fix**: Extend FR-013 so that missing required tools (the Claude Code CLI; curl for
    backend-dev; the Playwright MCP server for frontend-dev) are checked before planning and stop
    the run with an input error that names the tool.
- [ ] CHK038 - Is git commit behavior (U-6) either specified or explicitly excluded, given that commits affect recovery and controlled change? [Gap, Plan U-6]
  - **Recommended fix**: Add to Out of Scope or Assumptions: "Loops do not create version-control
    commits unless configured to; committing is the developer's responsibility."

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Suggested order: CHK008, CHK014–CHK018 (consistency fixes are cheap), then CHK001–CHK007 and
  CHK023 (execution and safety gaps), then the rest
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
